source_fields.formulation: Multiple clients face separate linear losses and exchange information only at prescribed synchronization rounds. Each client simultaneously queries two values of its current local function, and both query points incur loss. The comparator is one fixed point shared by all clients.
source_fields.solution_goal: Minimize performance as defined by the metric, guarantee, and native resource.

source_fields.instance: There are $M$ clients interacting simultaneously in $\mathbb R^d$ for $T=L_{\mathrm{comm}}R_{\mathrm{comm}}$ rounds each. They synchronize once every $L_{\mathrm{comm}}$ rounds, for $R_{\mathrm{comm}}$ synchronizations. $$f_t^m(x)=\langle g_t^m,x\rangle+b_t^m,\qquad \|g_t^m\|_2\le G.$$ $$f_t(x)=\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}f_t^m(x),\qquad \frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}\|\nabla f_t^m(x)-\nabla f_t(x)\|_2^2\le\zeta^2\quad(\forall t,x).$$ The adversary may depend on all past actions and the algorithm, but not on current private randomness. All clients share the same hindsight comparator: $$x^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\|x\|_2\le B}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{m=1}^{M}f_t^m(x).$$

operations.query_signature: Each client simultaneously submits $x_t^{m,1},x_t^{m,2}\in\mathbb R^d$ and receives exact values of the same current local function at both points. The second point cannot depend on the first response. There is no independent measurement noise; variance from randomized directions is part of the estimator analysis. Both query points incur loss. The comparator ball $\{x:\|x\|_2\le B\}$ does not restrict all queries. Inputs $M,d,T,L_{\mathrm{comm}},R_{\mathrm{comm}},G,B,\zeta$ are public. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

source_fields.feasibility: Each client outputs two simultaneous query points $x_t^{m,1},x_t^{m,2}\in\mathbb R^d$ per round, and both incur local loss. The comparator constraint $\|x\|_2\le B$ does not constrain these query points. Loss cannot be recomputed afterward at their center or average.
source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Previously executed online actions cannot be changed.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: No function value, optimality certificate, or final recommendation is required unless explicitly listed for this axis.

source_fields.normalization: Sum over the 2MT query points that actually incur loss, divide by 2MT, and then take expectation.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: The upper-bound strategy controls its queries and step sizes to ensure finite average expected regret. Full-space probes themselves do not have a uniform absolute-loss bound.

source_fields.adaptivity: Strictly follows the per-round and within-batch protocol of the oracle
restrictions: Between synchronizations, each client uses only its new local observations and history shared at the previous synchronization. Synchronization occurs every $L_{\mathrm{comm}}$ rounds, with no message-length bound.
Between synchronizations, clients use only new local observations and information shared at the preceding synchronization. Complete states or observations may be exchanged at synchronization.
Communication bits are neither bounded nor charged. A finite number of synchronizations does not imply bounded message length.

Private randomization is allowed, with the seed independent of the fixed instance and future external samples. Internal arithmetic, memory, linear spans, and iteration forms are unrestricted except for the stated computation, communication, privacy, and within-round interaction limits.
source_fields.internal_computation: Unrestricted except for explicit polynomial-time or protocol constraints
source_fields.parallelism: Follows the simultaneous-query, task-batch, and communication timing specified by the oracle

source_fields.complete_expression: This is average regret per actual query point. Multiply by $2MT$ for total two-point regret. Expectation includes randomized queries, with worst case over admissible adaptive loss environments.
aggregation_order: This is average regret per actual query point. Multiply by $2MT$ for total two-point regret. Expectation includes randomized queries, with worst case over admissible adaptive loss environments.
source_fields.quantifier_order: One admissible algorithm using only public information must handle every prescribed instance; adaptation to unknown budgets must be performed by that same algorithm.
randomness_sources: Observation or environment randomness explicitly allowed by the oracle.
source_fields.runtime_guarantee: The resource budget is fixed. Expected error is not automatically converted to high probability or a random-runtime bound.
